correctness.rationale: Both pointwise formulas are exact vertex-enumeration identities: the scalar max identity and l1 crosspolytope give F1=2-min|xi|; cube corners give F_infty=1+(a1+a2)/2. The infima and all minimizers follow from coordinate simplex constraints. Deviation mass balance proves the two sharp distance-to-uniform-orbit bounds, with explicit full-deficit equality families; a two-largest-coordinate argument proves the exact cube-vertex distance. Explicit orthogonal-coordinate pairs show A2=2 on both spaces. An exact-rational checker tests formulas/equality witnesses, supplementary to the analytic argument.
risks: The result is restricted to finite-dimensional real l1/l-infinity; quantitative constants depend on the definition of the mean with factor 1/2.
The finite checker is not used as a proof for all dimensions or vectors.

value.rationale: The lower Minkowski-ellipse constant is source-defined and geometrically motivated. The finding gives both complete pointwise profiles on a natural classical dual pair, proves a dimension-growing failure of duality invisible to the shared A2 value, classifies radically different extremizing sets (uniform vectors versus coordinate vertices), and supplies exact quantitative distance-to-minimizer stability with optimal coefficients for every deficit. These are natural structural distinctions and robustness statements, not isolated arbitrary instances.
risks: No universal sharp duality-gap theorem is asserted; only this exact canonical family is classified.
